evals.prompt: I want to add a team invitation feature with email invites, expiration times, and invitation revocation.
evals.expected_output: The run should classify this as a new feature and multi-step behavior change, choose feature alignment flow, identify goals, non-goals, affected surfaces, acceptance criteria, and verification, ask only questions that affect behavior or risk, produce a concise spec, and wait for explicit user confirmation before product-source edits when material invitation behavior remains inferred.
expectations: The run selects feature alignment flow for a multi-step feature
The run identifies goals, non-goals, affected behavior, acceptance criteria, and verification before implementation
The run asks only material questions and produces a concise spec before coding
The run waits for explicit confirmation when material invitation behavior remains inferred
The run does not require an external workflow backend before implementation

evals.prompt: The login page returns a 500 when I click submit. Please fix it.
evals.expected_output: The run should classify this as a lightweight bugfix, reproduce or inspect the failure before fixing, add a regression test first when practical, repair the smallest responsible boundary, and run targeted verification. It should not require feature alignment unless the bug reveals durable behavior or constraints.
expectations: The run selects the lightweight bugfix flow rather than full spec flow
The run investigates and reproduces before proposing a fix
The run adds or plans a regression test before implementation when practical

evals.prompt: The billing rule we agreed on just changed: trial users should also be included in usage statistics. Continue coding.
evals.expected_output: The run should detect a requirement change during coding, decide that it affects behavior, update task context or ask for alignment before continuing, and keep TDD and verification requirements in place.
expectations: The run detects that the prompt changes an approved requirement
The run updates task context or asks for alignment before continuing because behavior changed
The run keeps TDD and verification requirements after the requirement change

evals.prompt: This is simple, just change it directly: add an export data button to the user settings page.
evals.expected_output: The run should still recognize this as a user-visible feature, use a thin feature alignment flow, clarify button behavior, data scope, permissions, and verification, produce a concise spec, and wait for explicit confirmation before product-source edits because material export behavior remains unresolved. It should not skip alignment just because the user called it simple.
expectations: The run does not skip behavior alignment merely because the user calls a feature simple
The run asks material questions and produces a concise spec before coding
The run waits for explicit user confirmation and does not edit product source while export behavior remains unresolved

evals.prompt: $DDev has clarified the requirement boundary. Now call the coding flow to implement it and return evidence to DDev when done.
evals.expected_output: The run should recognize that it is being invoked as the DDev coding-flow module, implement according to the acceptance criteria and verification plan, use TDD or regression tests when practical, record tests and verification evidence, and return control to ddev rather than taking over delivery or durable memory.
expectations: The run treats spec-driven-coding as a DDev module when invoked by DDev
The run follows the acceptance criteria and verification plan
The run records tests or evidence before completion
The run returns lifecycle control to ddev after coding evidence
The run does not independently commit, push, or write durable memory unless requested

evals.prompt: Change the existing Add button label to New and keep its behavior exactly the same.
evals.expected_output: The run should classify this as a fully specified mechanical edit rather than an underspecified feature, record confirmation_not_required with the user's request as the acceptance source, make only the label change, and run focused verification without inventing a spec approval pause.
expectations: The run classifies the request as a mechanical edit with no unresolved material product behavior
The run records or plans confirmation_not_required with the user request as the acceptance source
The run does not ask for unnecessary feature approval
The run limits implementation and verification to the label change

evals.prompt: Implement a browser-only todo list in the existing Tools page. Store items in localStorage, support add, complete, and delete, and choose the reversible interaction details yourself.
evals.expected_output: The run should choose feature alignment flow, recognize that the user defined the material scope and explicitly delegated only reversible low-risk interaction details, state a concise spec and chosen assumptions, record confirmation_not_required with the user request as the primary acceptance source, and proceed without another approval pause while preserving the stated boundaries.
expectations: The run selects feature alignment flow and states a concise spec
The run recognizes that placement, persistence, and supported actions are already defined by the user
The run treats only reversible low-risk interaction details as delegated
The run records or plans confirmation_not_required with a clear source and reason
The run proceeds without an unnecessary confirmation pause and stays within the stated behavior

evals.prompt: Review the todo list implementation plan and point out missing requirements. Do not edit any files.
evals.expected_output: The run should select no coding flow, review the plan and missing requirements, and avoid source edits or an implementation workflow because the user explicitly requested read-only analysis.
expectations: The run selects no coding flow
The run identifies missing requirements without implementing them
The run does not edit files
